fun_facts: His family nickname since childhood was “Pookie.”
At 15, Jaxon Smith-Njigba played varsity football and led his team with 1,328 receiving yards in 12 games.
In the Rose Bowl, he caught 15 passes for 347 yards and three touchdowns; his 15 catches set a Rose Bowl record.
In 2021, he set a Big Ten record with 1,606 receiving yards.
In 2025, he earned first-team All-Pro honors after setting career highs of 119 catches, 1,793 receiving yards, and 10 touchdown catches.

## When [Jaxon Smith-Njigba](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4430878/jaxon-smith-njigba) needed a ride, 'Pookie' found a way

Rodney Webb, head coach of the Rockwall [Texas] High School football team, isn't exactly sure where Jaxon Smith-Njigba's nickname came from, but it still makes him smile. Webb and those who have known Smith-Njigba since he was an adolescent call him Pookie -- a family nickname since his childhood, and one his brother used in a video aired on the night the Seahawks selected him with the 20th pick in the 2023 draft.

When Jaxon Smith-Njigba commits to something, he pursues that goal to the fullest.

citations.title: Ohio State's Jaxon Smith-Njigba headed to draft, out for CFP - ESPN

excerpts:
Smith-Njigba, 24, set career highs in receptions (119), receiving yards (1,793) and touchdown receptions (10) en route to being named a first-team All-Pro in 2025. In three postseason games, he had 17 catches for 199 yards and two touchdowns.

Drafted 20th overall in 2023, Smith-Njigba finished his rookie season with 628 receiving yards before breaking out in Year 2 with 1,130, earning a Pro Bowl berth as an alternate.
